profileClaims.text: Daniel Bedrack is an AI and Automation Developer and Technical Project Manager.
He turns complex business processes into reliable automation systems by combining hands-on development with end-to-end technical project management.
Daniel is based in Israel and is open to full-time opportunities.

experience.role: Automation Developer and Technical Project Manager

claims.text: Daniel worked at Optimate from March 2025 through September 2026; this is previous, not current, employment.
Daniel worked as a Delivery Advisor at Tesla from February 2024 through March 2025.
Daniel provided coding support and reviewed assignments at Sela College from March 2023 through February 2024.

skills.text: Business-process automation, systems integration, workflow design, testing, implementation and operational support.
Hands-on work with Make.com, Fireberry CRM, monday.com, Gmail, Priority, VoiceCenter and ManyChat.
Applied AI experience includes document classification, structured information extraction, OCR workflows and AI-assisted software development.
Software-development foundations include React, React Native, Expo, TypeScript, Firebase and web application delivery.

summaryClaims.text: The project created an integrated operational ecosystem for apartment-interest leads, customers, apartments, contracts and cross-department workflows at the real-estate company Megureit.
The primary challenge was maintaining reliable Fireberry-Priority synchronization while live data continued to grow and change.

responsibilityClaims.text: Daniel led discovery, process characterization, CRM design and configuration, integrations, testing, training, implementation and ongoing support.
Reliability techniques included unique identifiers, duplicate prevention, bidirectional updates, logging, error handling and retry mechanisms.

technologyClaims.text: The system used Fireberry CRM, Priority, VoiceCenter, ManyChat, Make.com and iframe screens that improved usability.

outcomeClaims.text: The project centralized information, reduced duplicate entry and operational errors, improved tracking and created a shared operational view.

collaborationBoundaries.text: One additional developer assisted with Fireberry-Priority synchronization and iframe screens; Daniel's ownership must not erase that contribution.

verificationLimits.text: No exact outcome metrics are approved; outcomes must remain qualitative unless later evidence is supplied.
The repository is private, and no credentials, customer data or private implementation artifacts may be disclosed.

financialDocumentAutomation.title: AI-Powered Financial Document Processing for a Solar Energy Company

summaryClaims.text: The workflow replaced manual Gmail searching and attachment organization with OCR and AI classification, extraction and structured monday.com items for human review and approval.

responsibilityClaims.text: Daniel owned business analysis, solution design, development, testing, delivery and deployment.
He addressed inaccurate extraction through prompt refinement and required-field validation.

technologyClaims.text: Approved technologies are Make.com, Gmail, monday.com, OpenAI and OCR.

outcomeClaims.text: The employee's task changed from manual inbox organization to reviewing structured records and approving consequential actions.

verificationLimits.text: The solar-energy client name is confidential.
Google Cloud Vision is only a probable OCR provider and must not be stated as fact until Daniel verifies it.
No time-saving or document-volume metric is approved.

summaryClaims.text: RemindMe helps people remember small purchases by associating shopping items with store categories and notifying them near relevant stores, optionally while moving toward home.

responsibilityClaims.text: Daniel designed an adaptive speech-processing layer with multi-item parsing, quantities and units, a personal correction dictionary and a local Whisper Tiny fallback.
Daniel did not train a speech-recognition model; he built a processing layer around limitations in free speech-recognition services and tested it with his own Hebrew speech.

technologyClaims.text: The application uses Expo, React Native, web support, Firebase Authentication, Firestore and OpenStreetMap-based location discovery.
Repository-supported capabilities include configurable notification radius, GPS-noise rejection, list, map, history and profile views, English, Hebrew and Spanish localization, and RTL support.

outcomeClaims.text: On 18 October 2026, 27 automated tests, TypeScript checking and the web production export passed, and the public demo returned HTTP 200.

collaborationBoundaries.text: Daniel designed and developed RemindMe independently using an AI-assisted development workflow with OpenAI Codex.

verificationLimits.text: Reliable background notifications have not been verified on a real Android or iPhone device.
Final native identifiers and mobile authentication configuration are not verified as completed.
